claims.text: Torsion is time-critical: if findings strongly suggest it, go straight to surgical exploration rather than testing.
claims.quote: Timely diagnosis of testicular torsion is critical. If findings are highly suggestive of torsion, immediate surgical exploration is done in preference to testing.

claims.text: Equivocal, with no clear other cause: color Doppler ultrasound; radionuclide scan if Doppler isn't available (less sensitive and specific).
claims.quote: If findings are equivocal and there is no clear alternate cause of acute scrotal pain, color Doppler ultrasonography is done. If Doppler ultrasonography is not available, radionuclide scanning may be used but is less sensitive and specific.

claims.text: Urinalysis and culture in everyone; UTI findings suggest epididymitis.
claims.quote: Urinalysis and culture are always required. Findings of urinary tract infection (UTI—eg, pyuria, bacteriuria) suggest epididymitis.

claims.text: STI testing with UTI findings, urethral discharge or dysuria.
claims.quote: Patients with findings that suggest UTI and patients with urethral discharge or dysuria should be tested for STIs as well as other bacterial causes of UTI.

claims.text: Painful scrotal erythema with nontender testes: think cellulitis or early Fournier gangrene.
claims.quote: Painful erythema of the scrotum with no tenderness of the testes or epididymides should raise suspicion of infection, either cellulitis or early Fournier gangrene.
